title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is Grothendieck's study of the 'equation of loops' (équation des lacets), which yields the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group he calls M. The profinite modular group is SL2(Z)^, or modulo ±1 it is PSL2(Z)^ = Z/2 * Z/3 completed. It has elliptic generators: ρ of order 3 (order 6 in SL2) and σ of order 2 (order 4 in SL2). L_ρ and L_σ are the finite cyclic subgroups they generate, so L_ρ/{±1} ≅ Z/3 and L_σ/{±1} ≅ Z/2. N_ρ^* and N_σ^* are normalizers of these subgroups inside a large group Z^!_{ρ,σ}. On the next page this group is written M[0] = M(0)·L_0^! = Norm_{M^!}(L_0), where M^! = M(0)·Π is an extension of Grothendieck's group M (the GT-like group, his model for Γ_Q) by the profinite fundamental group. Γ_{ρ,σ} (written γ here) is identified with Π̃_Q (≅ Γ̃_Q) ≅ M(0), an extended 'arithmetic' group.

Previous page. Restricting the two homomorphisms (123), Z^!_{ρ,σ} → N_ρ^*/±1 and Z^!_{ρ,σ} → N_σ^*, to the subgroup L_0^π gives:
- the map to N_ρ^*/±1 is trivial;
- the map to N_σ^* factors through L_0^π/L_0^{π_0} ≅ μ = Z/2, sending the generator to −1 (see (128), (129)).

This page.
1. Passing to the quotient, he gets two canonical homomorphisms (130): Γ_{ρ,σ} = Π̃_Q → N_ρ^*/±1 and Γ_{ρ,σ} → N_σ^*/±1.
2. These are sections of the natural projections N_ρ^*/±1 → Γ_{ρ,σ} and N_σ^*/±1 → Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ M(0). The projections have kernels L_ρ/±1 and L_σ/±1.
3. Hence semidirect product decompositions (131):
   - N_ρ^*/±1 ≅ Γ_{ρ,σ} ⋉ Z/3;
   - N_σ^*/±1 ≅ Γ_{ρ,σ} ⋉ Z/2.
4. Γ acts on Z/3 through the quadratic character ε_3, i.e. the mod-3 cyclotomic character (the character of Q(√−3)): a Galois-type element sends ρ to a conjugate of ρ^{χ(g)}. On the σ side the action is said to be 'given by ε_2' (the mod-4 character, Q(i)).
5. He remarks that the symmetry between the two sides is 'boiteuse' (lopsided). The σ-side map lifts canonically to (132) Π̃_Q = Γ_{ρ,σ} → N_σ^* itself, not just mod ±1. The lift goes through M(0) ⊂ M[0] = Z^!, using that M(0) ↪ Z^! → N_σ^*.
6. The next page reformulates this: Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ M_0^![0]/L_0^{Π_0}, a splitting of 1 → L_σ → N_σ^* → Γ → 1, and an explicit description (134) of the section's image.

Purpose. This is a group-theoretic version, for the GT-type group M, of the fact that Gal(Q̄/Q) acts on the elliptic (torsion) subgroups of the profinite modular group by conjugation composed with the cyclotomic character. It also shows that the normalizers of the order-3 and order-4 torsion split over the arithmetic group. It is analogous to the GT action x ↦ x^λ, y ↦ f^{-1} y^λ f restricted to the elliptic generators.
errors: The claim that Γ_{ρ,σ} acts on L_σ/{±1} ≅ Z/2Z 'via the quadratic character ε_2' is vacuous: Aut(Z/2) is trivial, so the semidirect product N_σ^*/±1 ≅ Γ·Z/2 is in fact direct. The meaningful statement is presumably the action on L_σ ≅ Z/4 itself (via the mod-4 character), which is what the lift (132) to N_σ^* captures.

The semidirect product decompositions rely on the sections in (130) being well defined, i.e. on the triviality and factorisation statements from the previous page (restriction of (123) to L_0^π). These are asserted from characterisation (122) with sketchy justification ('car ... mod π^'), not fully proved on the page.

ideas.what: Canonical splitting of the normalizers of the order-3 and order-4 (or order-2 mod ±1) elliptic subgroups of the profinite modular group over the arithmetic (GT-type) group, giving semidirect products
ideas.modern_name: Normalizers of finite subgroups of SL2(Z)^ / PSL2(Z)^ under the GT or Galois action; torsion in the extended profinite modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Ihara (actions of GT and Galois on profinite braid and mapping class groups, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse; the GT-action on elliptic generators is implicit in Drinfeld/Ihara-style formulas (x ↦ x^λ)

ideas.what: Action of the arithmetic group on the cyclic elliptic subgroups via cyclotomic characters mod 3 and mod 4 (ε_3, ε_2)
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on torsion of the modular group through the cyclotomic character (CM points j=0, j=1728)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Ihara, Nakamura; also Deligne's tangential basepoints)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of SL2(Z)^ and the points of order 2 and 3)

ideas.what: Observation that the σ-side section lifts canonically to N_σ^* (not just mod ±1) via M(0) ⊂ M[0]=Z^!, breaking the ρ/σ symmetry
ideas.modern_name: Lifting of the GT/Galois action from PSL2^ to SL2^ (central extension by ±1)

deep.surprise_reason: These are technical intermediate lemmas in Grothendieck's GT-type construction: normalizer splittings with cyclotomic action on elliptic torsion. They are consistent with, and essentially contained in, known results on the GT/Galois action on the profinite modular group. Nothing here appears to be a missed result.
transcription_corrections: 'γ_{ρ,σ}' should likely be read as Γ_{ρ,σ}, consistent with the next page.
The group written 'Γ̃_Q' in (130) and (132) looks in the image more like Π̃_Q (Π with tilde, index Q). The next page's 'Π_φ^~' is likely the same symbol Π̃_Q.
In (131) the struck-out symbol after γ_{ρ,σ} is a deleted '∗'; the product is a semidirect product.
The final line under (132) reads '≃ M(0) ⊂ M[0] = Z^!', with arrows indicating that the lift factors through M(0).
